laser_cooling_scheme.summary: ground a8S7/2 --460 nm--> y8P9/2 --leak--> a10D9/2, a10D11/2 --507/513 nm via y10P11/2--> a10D13/2; Zeeman slowing + yellow MOT on a10D13/2 - z10F15/2 (583 nm); pump-back with 609 nm (a10D13/2 - z10F13/2) and 1204 nm (a10D11/2 - y8P9/2); red MOT on a8S7/2 - z10P9/2 (687 nm) with repumpers at 1148, 1171, 1204 nm (five hyperfine components); evaporation in a 1550 nm crossed dipole trap to BEC of 151Eu

583 nm natural linewidth: 8.2 MHz (Inoue 2018, Miyazawa 2021, Matsui 2021) vs 8.3 MHz (Miyazawa 2017); both derive from the Den Hartog lifetime 19.5(1.0) ns (-> 8.16 MHz).
460 nm natural linewidth: Kozuma group quotes 27 MHz; Den Hartog lifetime 6.1(3) ns gives 26.1 MHz and A = 1.61(8)e8 s^-1 gives 25.6 MHz.

y8P lifetimes: Den Hartog LIF values 6.6/6.4/6.1 ns (J=5/2,7/2,9/2) agree with Meyer 1981 LIF but the resonance-broadening (Penkin & Shabanova 1973: 6.45/5.68/5.46 ns) and Hanle (Handrich 1969: 6.7/5.8/5.5 ns) values are up to 10 % shorter; all kept under lifetime_other.
z8P9/2, z6P7/2 lifetimes: Hanle values of Kretzen 1969 (810(100), 670(70) ns) are well below the LIF values (1045(52), 870(44) ns).
notes: Lifetimes (85 levels, Table 1) and transition probabilities (140 lines, Table 4) were parsed from the text layer of the publisher PDF of Den Hartog et al. 2002 retrieved through the Internet Archive (iopscience.iop.org itself is bot-blocked); the +- signs are lost in the text layer but value/uncertainty pairs are unambiguous, and the count of parsed rows (85, 140) matches the numbers stated in the abstract. Den Hartog level energies are those of Martin, Zalubas, Hagan (1978) and coincide with the NIST energies used as identifiers. NIST ASD already carries the Den Hartog A values (same numbers); they are repeated here with their uncertainties. rme_J_ea0 entries are derived from the measured A with the SCHEMA convention. Hyperfine constants follow E = A K/2 + B [3K(K+1)/4 - I(I+1)J(J+1)] / [2I(2I-1)J(2J-1)]; both ground-state A values are negative.
